svg.text: In this stretch, at the median: the draw takes 5.40 ms on the CPU, the GPU works 7.49 ms on a frame, and a frame is shown 34.70 ms after its start. 2 on screen longer than asked, 2 of 16 animation errors of 1 ms or more, 1 reported without a display time.
The refresh grid is the vertical blank times the application read on its CPU clock. Display times are what the graphics driver reported, not a measurement by the tools.
A stage the log has no times for is not drawn. In a viewer that shows an SVG's tooltips, a shape under the pointer gives its times and details.

The thin lines follow a frame: from the CPU thread (its submit, where the log has one) to its GPU work, from its present call down to its row of the wait to be shown, from the end of its GPU work to the start of that wait, and from there to the screen.
A frame reported without a display time may or may not have been shown: the time it would have been on screen is drawn as not known, and only a capture settles it.
The animation error of a shown frame is its animation time step minus its display time step from the frame before, by the reported display times; it is not known after a frame without one.

The pacer's lanes: the work it was given for a frame (CPU plus the newest GPU time the application had) as a length in the frame time it had, and the late frames in its frame window as a share of the count the rule slows down at (its default settings).
The lane by animation time has each frame from its animation time to the next frame's: when the animation expected it on screen. The animation clock is tied to the display at #117's display time.
In that lane a frame's animation error is how far its box moved against its place on the display, compared with the frame before.
